def count_capped_sequences(n, m, L, d):
    """Count sequences (a_1, ..., a_n) with every a_i an integer in {1, ..., m}
    that satisfy BOTH conditions:

      1. No run of equal consecutive values is longer than L (a "run" is a
         maximal block of adjacent equal values).
      2. Exactly d distinct values appear somewhere in the sequence.

    Return the exact count as a Python int (no modulus; the result can be
    astronomically large).

    Input domain: 1 <= n <= 100, 1 <= m <= 50, 1 <= L <= n, 1 <= d <= m.
    All arguments are ints. Note d may exceed n, in which case the answer
    is 0 (a length-n sequence cannot contain more than n distinct values).
    Other impossible combinations (e.g. d == 1 with n > L) also return 0.

    Examples:
    >>> count_capped_sequences(2, 2, 1, 2)
    2
    >>> count_capped_sequences(3, 2, 2, 2)
    6
    >>> count_capped_sequences(4, 3, 2, 2)
    30
    """
